doc.title: Ron Carter interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999

title: Gigging around upstate New York while at Eastman
summary: Carter played the Pythodd Room and towns along the Thruway on weekends, driving back for Monday theory class.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I started the process there, yes, over on the — way across town from the school, the physical location. And I’d play there two or three nights a week or go out to Syracuse or Utica. There’s a trunkline — at that time — a trunkline from Canada to New York, which is kind of on the Thruway, because of the Thruway route. Utica, Little Falls, Herkimer, Syracuse, Rochester, Buffalo and it ends in New York. And so I’d be making gigs up there in most of the towns on weekends, and driving back to school for an eight o’clock theory class Monday morning.
It’s an accomplishment that you made it through that kind of schedule.
Well you don’t think it’s difficult, it’s the only way to get it done.
